title: Ordinary ringed pullback transports stratified perfect local models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $C_{n,W}=(R/t^n)_W$ for $n\geq1$ and $B_W=\varprojlim_n C_{n,W}$ with projections $\pi_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the coefficient map $c_f:f^{-1}B_Y\to B_X$ characterized by $\pi_{X,n}c_f=c^f_{R/t^n}f^{-1}(\pi_{Y,n})$, where $c^f_{R/t^n}$ is the constant-section structure map [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $f_B^*Q=B_X\otimes_{f^{-1}B_Y}f^{-1}Q$ be ordinary module pullback, applied termwise to complexes, and let $P_f=Lf_B^*$ with its canonical K-flat computation counit $\epsilon_Q:P_f[Q]\to[f_B^*Q]$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Here $[Q]$ denotes localization of a complex in the ordinary unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; tensors are sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

Assume $X,Y$ are noetherian, meaning locally noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact. Let $K\in D(B_Y)$, let $i_i:S_i\hookrightarrow Y$ be a finite constructible locally closed stratification [def-constructible-stratification], and suppose that there are pro-etale covers $\{U_{ia}\to S_i\}_a$ and bounded complexes $L_{ia}^{\bullet}$ of finite projective $R$-modules such that $i_i^*K|_{U_{ia}}\simeq B_{U_{ia}}\otimes_R L_{ia}^{\bullet}$. Finite projective means a direct summand of a finite free module; ordinary exact immersion restriction is meant [lem-sf-immersion-completed-pullback-comparison].

Set $X_i=X\times_Y S_i$, $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$, $f_i:X_i\to S_i$, and $V_{ia}=X_i\times_{S_i}U_{ia}$, with projection $v_{ia}:V_{ia}\to U_{ia}$. After discarding empty $X_i$, the $j_i$ form a finite constructible locally closed stratification of $X$, and $\{V_{ia}\to X_i\}_a$ are pro-etale covers. The coefficient structural maps of the equal composites $fj_i=i_if_i$ agree under the inverse-image composition isomorphisms, as do all their finite projections. The canonical ordinary derived composition and slice-restriction comparisons give
$$j_i^*P_fK\simeq P_{f_i}(i_i^*K),\qquad
(j_i^*P_fK)|_{V_{ia}}\simeq P_{v_{ia}}(B_{U_{ia}}\otimes_R L_{ia}^{\bullet})\simeq B_{V_{ia}}\otimes_R L_{ia}^{\bullet}.$$
The last isomorphism is computed termwise on each bounded finite-projective model: it sends a pulled free basis vector to the same basis vector and restricts by the same idempotent to every finite-projective summand. These are the ordinary ringed comparisons, before taking any completion; no completeness assumption on $P_fK$, no flatness or invertibility of $c_f$, and no separatedness or base-field linearity of $f$ is assumed.

proof.text: Construct the nonempty pullback-stratum index set I = { i : Fin n | Nonempty (X times_Y S_i) } and enumerate it by Fintype.equivFin. Define each stratum directly as f-preimage of the original stratum, with its pullback scheme and pullback.fst immersion. Local closedness, disjointness, constructibility and the range equation follow from continuous preimage, [lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage], and the pullback range formula. For coverage, any point x over a stratum gives a point of that pullback by the range formula, hence its index lies in I. This includes empty schemes and the empty index set. Apply the cover-preserving pro-etale base-change functor of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] to each original covering sieve. Pull back along its invertible terminal comparison and use uniqueness of maps into the terminal object to identify the arrows with the displayed terminal arrows. This gives the covering clause for every i, without using the nonempty hypothesis.

proof.text: For coefficientMap_comp, use the direct-image constant-map composition calculation in [lem-tw-completed-coefficient-ringed-coherence] at every quotient R/t^(n+1), then forget commutativity. The projection specification in [def-sf-ordinary-integral-pullback-construction] shows that the composite completed direct-image map has the same projections as the map of the composite morphism; uniqueness makes them equal. Taking adjunction mates through the specified geometric direct-image compositor gives exactly inverseComp and the completed inverse-image composition equation. Adjunction naturality also gives every displayed finite projection equation. The slice coherence remains the declared input to the ordinary chart-comparison step.

proof.text: Construct moduleSquare_existsUnique directly from the already proved coefficient direct-image composition equation. The sectionwise module pushforward composition comparisons, for the two equal composites of the pullback square, give a right-adjoint isomorphism. On sections it is precisely restriction along squareSite. Take its adjunction mate for the two composite ordinary pullback adjunctions. The composite-unit equation gives the prescribed iterated-generator normalization. Applying the composite adjunction hom equivalence and checking sections proves uniqueness. For derivedSquare_existsUnique, package the existing ordinary computation counits as natural transformations. Their components are invertible by the exact ordinary pullback result [lem-tw-ordinary-completed-pullback-exact], transferred to the specified original ordinary pullback by the projection uniqueness in [def-sf-ordinary-integral-pullback-construction]. The two iterated counit comparisons, followed on one side by complexSquare, give an isomorphism after precomposition with the cochain localization. Mathlib Localization.liftNatIso descends it. Its component formula is exactly the required counit equation. Cancellation against the invertible iterated counit and Localization.natTrans_ext prove uniqueness. Applying the two resulting squares constructs localExchange, and applying ordinary pullback to the given chart isomorphism gives its middle factor.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition, and Tag 06YY; ordinary adjunction mates are Stacks sites-modules.tex Tags 03D1 and 03D2. Exact localization specialization using the existing exactness input.

proof.text: For modelPullback_existsUnique, identify the selected modelModule with the concrete scalarPerfectFunctor, naturally in every scalar module. The object and map specifications of derived change of rings supply the first comparison, and identity component maps compare the old and independent-universe tensor presheaves. Naturality of abelian sheafification proves that this isomorphism carries modelSection(b,x) to the same pure tensor. Transport the already proved allComparison from [lem-tw-finite-projective-model-pullback] through these natural isomorphisms. Naturality of the specified ordinary pullback adjunction unit transports its generator normalization. For uniqueness, precompose with the inverse model isomorphism and use the constant-model/terminal-section adjunction: values on terminal constant generators determine each transpose, and the ordinary pullback Hom equivalence is injective. This applies to every scalar module, including zero modules and empty schemes; no finite-projectivity hypothesis is introduced.

source.place: Tags 03CY and 03EK; existing normalized scalar-model adjunction proof in lem-tw-finite-projective-model-pullback, transported through the selected tensor functor specifications.

proof.text: For perfectModelPullback, construct the finite-projective scalar realization using the existing scalarPerfectFunctor. The constant-unit and scalar-extension-unit comparisons from [lem-sfb-scalar-perfect-chart-finite-free], additivity and preservation of finite products identify its realization of R^(Fin n) with B^(Fin n). A finite projective scalar module is a retract of such a module. Apply the finite-free retract flatness calculation of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-ringed-pullback-model]. The object specification of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] identifies the original selected modelModule objects with the same tensor construction; identity component maps and tensor induction check restriction maps. Transfer flatness across this isomorphism. The original upper bound is preserved by the additive realization. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] and the original computation-counit theorem in [def-sf-ordinary-integral-pullback-construction]. Compose its invertible counit with localization of modelPullbackComplex. The main theorem then composes localExchange, the functor image of the given chart isomorphism, and this invertible counit/model composite. The generator-normalized model and square comparison theorems remain named intermediate statements of this module.

proof.text: Additivity of modelModule is the composite of constant-module additivity from [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] and the selected scalar-extension additivity. Its modelModule_obj equation is exactly the object specification of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], with the standard derived-category choices fixed as in completedConstantExtension. These proofs preserve the existing functors and their generator definitions.

proof.text: For immersionExact and weaklyEtaleExact, first identify the ringed chart direct map with ordinaryIntegralDirectRingMap. Apply the completed coefficient projection equation in [lem-tw-completed-coefficient-ringed-coherence], take its adjunction mate, forget commutativity and use the projection uniqueness of [def-sf-ordinary-integral-pullback-construction]. The induced pushforward isomorphism has a left-adjoint mate identifying the module pullbacks. Transfer the finite-limit theorem [lem-tw-ordinary-completed-pullback-exact] across this isomorphism. Finite colimits follow from the specified ordinary adjunction. An exact additive functor inverts homotopy quasi-isomorphisms after localization; its total left-derived counit is invertible by the universal property. Each factor in ordinaryIntegralPullComplexCounit is therefore invertible on every complex. Specialize to immersions and weakly etale morphisms. No completion or condition on the input complex is added.
